extracted.intended_audience: Reuters journalists, editors and newsroom production staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and production standards for writing, tagging and filing multiple Reuters story formats (e.g., Highlights, Interview, Analysis, Feature, Factbox, Polls, Top News). Covers tagging, length, sourcing, editorial approval, and technical filing conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIGHLIGHTS format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use HIGHLIGHTS to report running quotes or rapid-fire key points from events; tag headlines with HIGHLIGHTS and include HIGHLIGHTS in the slug and headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refresh HIGHLIGHTS frequently; use subheads (e.g. RATES, INFLATION, FX) to group ideas; add 'THIS ITEM WILL BE UPDATED' and remove when event ends; put an R in 'Message Type' to refresh; snaps are covered by an XREF to give access to rolling HIGHLIGHTS; change the USN frequently in a long series of snaps so corrections don't force repeating the whole sequence; use the HIGHLIGHTS tag at the start of the headline and give the item a slug with HIGHLIGHTS in brackets; production typically requires several people (one filing snaps, one checking, sub editor compiling, another filing XREFs). Editing desk: publish first version fast, file updates to same USN with R to overwrite, insert 'LATEST QUOTES' above 'EARLIER QUOTES' and keep important news at top, capitalise short subheads, watch length (130 lines maximum), not every snap must be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: XREFs for snaps and rolling coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use XREF entries to allow subscribers to access rolling HIGHLIGHTS/snaps via a double-click link to the USN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text in the XREF should describe the event and provide a click-through to the USN of the Highlights; if you need to change something in an XREF already filed, use 'O' not 'R' or you will lose all snaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking quotes selection and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Be selective with quotes: focus on key quotes rather than full transcripts and paraphrase long or non-snapty remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If speaker responds to a question include the question only when essential and paraphrase for brevity; paraphrase lengthy non-snap material; use brief summary headlines (e.g. DOLLAR OVERVALUED?) for speed and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview tagging and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve INTERVIEW tag/slug for substantive, prepared interviews with notable subjects; story should say the subject 'told Reuters' or 'said in an interview'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply INTERVIEW to shouted questions in a scrum; INTERVIEW can be used for notable fund managers but not routine views; prepare well and advise photo/video colleagues; EXCLUSIVE tag is for stories obtained solely by Reuters and of exceptional significance; strong interviews may also be filed as a TEXT of Q&A excerpts that repeats all quotes with questions and carries additional Q&A in order; interviews are not normally updated, but if subject discloses breaking news file an Alert/Urgent and later write the full INTERVIEW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsmaker / Obituary profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NEWSMAKER tag for topical profiles and OBITUARY when subject has died; aim for concise self-contained pen-portraits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for no more than 500 words (50 lines in Lynx Editor); make clear high up why the person is in the news; include essential personal details and precise dates; top half: concise summary of claim to fame with minimal biography, remainder: chronological career review; think colour and descriptive; keep Newsmakers on prominent personalities on file and update regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness stories standards
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person accounts by Reuters journalists of experiences or observations in which they participated, slugged WITNESS-XX/ and accompanied by an Advisory about the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow personality, feeling and engagement but not opinion, prejudice or partisanship; Reuters standards of impartiality and accuracy apply; illustrate with an image of the author and ideally related pictures; discuss with regional editors who will supervise production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brights / Odds (ODD) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Brights or 'odds' are stories reported because they are funny, quirky, bizarre, poignant or unusual and should carry the ODD slug and topic code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually about 300 words; work best with a telling quote and often end with a humorous detail; should be told straight without forcing adjectives; must be properly sourced and tasteful; consider whether it will interest a foreign reader; do not label a hard news story with bizarre elements as ODD if the reason to cover is serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis (ANALYSIS / INSIGHT) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: ANALYSIS pieces examine trends or developments and explore likely outcomes; INSIGHT should reveal something readers didn't know and include original reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should be informative, based on reportage with facts/data and quotes from sources, not mere author opinion; include authoritative named sources (except in exceptional circumstances); be fair and acknowledge counter-arguments; pitch to an editor before starting; typical length about 800 words (80 lines), exceptionally up to 1500 words with INSIGHT tag; on investment issues use real metrics (valuation, historical performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Snap Analysis format
rubrics_metrics.description: A bullet-point, rapid form of Analysis produced quickly after an event to provide immediate interpretation and insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to publish within 30 minutes of an event; written in bullet points with at least five bullets; can be bylined/datelined but not required; can be divided by sub-heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buy or Sell analysis format
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of Analysis offering contrasting views on the value of an individual company, currency, commodity or instrument — not a direct recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with 1–3 paragraphs; argument set under Buy and Sell sub-heads; refer to and use data (short interest, put-call ratios, price differentials, volumes, spreads etc.); use direct quotes and keep reported speech minimal; quote credible analysts/investors/traders (not fence-sitters); be succinct—try to keep under 500 words (50 lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: DEALTALK criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: DEALTALK offers exclusive details and insight on takeover, capital-raising or financial industry developments and incremental developments in ongoing transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEALTALK must be exclusive (not from press releases), include investment banks/financial players, be well-sourced and authoritative, be timely, well-written and engaging; be wary of banker spin and represent all viewpoints; use DEALTALK named item code and slug as DEALTALK/XXX and include ((For more Reuters DEALTALKs, click [DEALTALK/])).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature story standards
rubrics_metrics.description: FEATURE is an in-depth insight into a trend, issue or personality and must be accompanied by illustrative material (picture, graphic, video, factbox).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should enlighten readers, use specific examples and place them in a broad framework showing implications; be cross-sectoral appealing to a global audience; no editorialising; give dates for events; Features Editor approval required for an outline before proceeding; usual maximum ~1,000 words (100 lines) except with approval; slugline must indicate type (e.g., SCIENCE FEATURE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special reports / Enterprise reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Enterprise journalism: deeply reported stories, done on initiative, that otherwise would not come to light (investigative, exclusive looks, revelatory profiles, scoops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enterprise stories vary in time and length—may take days to months and can run to magazine length (~2,500 words); pitch ideas to bureau chief/editor-in-charge then send pitches to Enterprise Pitches distribution list; send finished enterprise stories to Enterprise Stories distribution list and cc relevant reporters/editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns are opinion pieces by appointed columnists, licensed to express a point of view and must carry a disclaimer that their views are not Reuters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contain a strong, reasoned argument backed by facts and solid reporting; be fair and acknowledge other viewpoints; avoid partisan invective; appointment and topic selection require Editor-in-Chief approval and close consultation with supervising editor; variations in tone/style are acceptable; label as COLUMN with topic code CLM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blogging dos and don'ts
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for Reuters bloggers to be engaging, conversational and to use blogging to add color, context and multimedia where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do be interesting, conversational, link to external relevant sites, monitor other bloggers, tag posts for search, show personality, use multimedia, credit original sources, have a second pair of eyes before publication, and ask desks to link to relevant stories. Don't be one-sided opinion, respond in anger to comments, end every post with 'tell us what you think', link to infringing material, let the color be subbed out, or take others' ideas without acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diaries / Calendar coding and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: National diaries should include news codes DIA and CAL; Diaries Desk assembles important items into subject-matter diaries monitored centrally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include DIA in a service message; mark new or amended national diary entries with an asterisk; add diary events as soon as possible; diary items should be text or tabular and queries to Diaries Desk sent to CAL LON; use IND/DIARY to see examples on Reuters 3000Xtra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factbox format
rubrics_metrics.description: FACTBOX presents clear, comparative information in short, graphic, bulletpoint form for background (people, countries, issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic factboxes normally run at a maximum of five key facts; other types (corporate boards, procedures) may use Q&A format; economic factboxes can be tabular; headline FACTBOX has no dateline (begin with date and signoff must include compiler's name and location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronology / Timeline conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronology/Timeline are forms of factbox listing events in chronological order related to a major news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep entries to essentials—usually no more than 10 key dates with one or two lines each; start with the oldest information first; no dateline; signoff must include compiler name and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q+A format
rubrics_metrics.description: Q+A is a factbox in question-and-answer style used to explain complicated issues and highlight depth of understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written in bullet-point formats; can be bylined and datelined but not required; headline tag Q+A and an example format provided in handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenarios format
rubrics_metrics.description: SCENARIOS is a factbox used to project possible outcomes of a crisis or situation, ideally giving probabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written in bullet points; can be bylined and datelined but not necessary; where possible give guidance on probability of each scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshot format
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAPSHOT is a quick, bullet-point summary for screen and media clients on a major story of global interest, usually updated regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally no longer than one A4 page; list latest developments, key quotes, main statistics and forthcoming events; assume reader has general understanding and dispense with most background; should only be compiled with decision by relevant regional editor; in commodities it may compile various market reports with click links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables present numerical or specialist data (results, indicators, bond issues, commodities) and may be quicker for specialist clients than text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label tables clearly and use TABLE tag; include 'T' in header field in System 77/Decade; write an active headline; organise tables logically and neatly; alignment is crucial (decimal points aligned, left alignment for text columns), keep columns equally spaced with 2–3 spaces between columns; file tables within 10 minutes of an Alert where required; complicated tables can be filed in pages with key numbers first and follow-up page later; results of important elections must be filed as a Table.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEXT item rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Clients want to read the text of major announcements or speeches; use TEXT (not FULL TEXT) as the headline tag and indicate whether it's full or partial text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original is not English say so and whether Reuters translation; TEXT may be filed in multiple 'takes'—use same slug and add page number with '=' (e.g., TEXT-... =2); strong interviews may be reported later as a TEXT of Q&A excerpts repeating all quotes and adding more Q&A in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top News summaries standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Top News pages serve as front pages for screen services and must be uniform, carefully curated and adhere to strict formatting and coding conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert news judgement required in choosing and ordering headlines—aim for no more than 12 stories; senior editors responsible for uniformity; all stories should be accessible to permissioned users and cross-references must work; include header codes TOP, GLANCE, XREF, unique USN and R in Message Type/Ref field; GLANCE/XXX and TOP/XXX named item codes in RIC/NI fields; headline must be upper and lower case; TOP NEWS in headline must be preceded and closed by a single asterisk; related markets links toolbar must appear under main headline and use vertical bars | to group links; never write an introduction to the TOP NEWS summary; story headlines grouped by 1–4 categories with first label 'Top Stories'; use > symbol before each story headline; never wrap a story headline to second line—truncate with ellipses; dynamic cross-reference links grouped under UP-TO-THE-MINUTE HEADLINES and LIVE PRICES & DATA; never exceed 2 columns of 2 cross reference links within a category; static Speedguides links at bottom should not change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polling (POLL) standards and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Poll stories must be exclusive Reuters polls and carry POLL tag; polls can establish consensus expectations and are often linked to events (use PRE code if linked to a future event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to poll: choose a clear subject; set clear, unambiguous and fair questions (no leading questions); find bona fide respondents; collect responses by phone/e-mail/fax; analyse responses—establish consensus using median (preferred to mean), publish highest/lowest and number of forecasts, consider mode; don't ignore mavericks; publish timing of the poll (dates conducted) for transparency and credibility; run individual responses when possible; polls on company earnings should carry EARNINGS POLL tag; contact Polling Unit for help.
